transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Head of Search, Maelstrom), Priya Desai (Lead ML Engineer), Carlos Mendes (CTO)

Auto-generated summary: Intro demo of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking. Q&A on latency/cost and security. Next steps agreed.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. we've got maya from our se team, she'll run through the technical demo. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Alex: good, thanks. excited to see how your hosted flow compares with our current setup, we've been testing a couple of vector stores and want to see rerank accuracy.
[00:20] Maya: great, i'll jump in. quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, the two-step retrieve-and-rerank pattern, then the console quick tour for Optimize and relevance tuning, and finally security notes.
[00:33] Priya: perfect. for context, we have ~1.2M docs, mix of long articles and short blurbs, currently using FAISS on a k8s cluster. our p95 latency target for search is ~250ms interactive. cost is also a big factor.
[00:46] Jordan: got it. and timeline for pilot?
[00:49] Carlos: we want a pilot in the next two weeks, product needs to sign off mid-feb if results look good.
[00:55] Maya: ok, jumping into the hosted API. so the embeddings endpoint supports variable dims — you can pick our tuned 1536 vector or larger models. we recommend matching dimensionality to your encoder; if you already have embeddings you can also upload vectors directly.
[01:10] Alex: quick question, can we use existing vector store (weaviate/FAISS) and only use your rerank?
[01:16] Maya: yes that's common. customers host their vector index and call Redwood for rerank only by sending top-k ids and the raw doc text, or we can run retrieval too if you want an all-hosted flow. there can be slight latency tradeoffs depending on network hops.
[01:30] Priya: curious about rerank cost model — is it per token for the reranker call or per request?
[01:36] Jordan: rerank is billed per-token on the model used, and the embeddings are billed per-vector unit. we'll share exact numbers in the pricing sheet. maya: on the infra side we've got continuous batching and KV cache for prefixes to reduce repeated token cost.
[01:52] Maya: demo time — showing a sample query against hosted embeddings + rerank. note: the console shows token breakdown, p50/p95 latency, and per-route cost.
[02:10] [screen share noise] Maya: here's the API call — embeddings create with model param, returns vector, then search returns candidate ids — then we call rerank with candidates and the original query as context.
[02:28] Alex: so in the two-step flow how many candidates do people usually send to rerank?
[02:33] Maya: typically 50-200 depending on cost vs recall. we demo 100 today. we also show an end-to-end with a small candidate set of 20 for low-latency cases.
[02:45] Priya: any built-in support for negative sampling or tuning the reranker?
[02:50] Maya: the Console Optimize has eval sets and you can run A/B comparisons, add labeled positives/negatives. it surfaces metrics like MRR and recall@k and suggests candidate sizes and model variants.
[03:05] Jordan: also worth mentioning our Optimize suggestions: batching, recommended quantization profile for common GPUs, and cache TTLs — those usually drop unit cost 30–60% in trials.
[03:18] Alex: that's promising. how disruptive is switching quantization — do models lose much quality?
[03:22] Maya: depends. we provide model-variant profiles from float16 down to int8/quantized combos. Optimize will flag quality regressions on your eval set. we've seen small regressions on generative quality but reranking tasks are usually robust to heavy quantization.
[03:40] Priya: about latency — our p95 includes vector retrieval and rerank. if we keep retrieval internal in our cluster and hit your rerank hosted, network RTT could add ~20–40ms depending on region?
[03:53] Maya: correct. you can also use our Dedicated or Private option if you need under-100ms regional SLAs; hosted is often fine for 100–300ms targets.
[04:05] Carlos: security is big for us. do you support SSO, SAML, and customer-managed KMS?
[04:12] Jordan: yes. we provide SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations. for Private deployments we support VPC peering or on-prem pattern and HSM/KMS key control. we'll share the SOC2 and architecture docs.
[04:26] Alex: any data retention or PII handling options?
[04:30] Maya: hosted API has configurable retention — you can opt-out of storing request payloads and enable encryption at rest. we also support redaction hooks in the client.
[04:40] Priya: good. can we control model version pinning? we need deterministic results for evaluation.
[04:45] Maya: yes, you can pin model versions and use rollouts. the console shows traffic split and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if a model becomes unavailable.
[04:56] Alex: demo the console Optimize recommendations?
[04:58] [screen share] Maya: sure — here's a prompt set with labeled queries, optimize suggests change candidate_set from 200 to 75, recommend int8 quantization on this model, and shows estimated cost per 1k queries. you can export the suggested config and apply as a route.
[05:20] Jordan: to be transparent about pricing, for rerank-heavy patterns we often recommend lowering candidate size and using a smaller rerank model; Optimize will show quality delta.
[05:30] Priya: what about concurrency — if we have bursts of 200 qps, will hosted handle that?
[05:34] Maya: hosted can autoscale but with some upper limits on burst capacity for standard accounts. Dedicated reserved capacity is recommended for consistent 100s+ qps with tighter SLOs. we can provision a pilot pool for your test.
[05:50] Alex: ok can you run a bench with our 1k queries and sample docs?
[05:54] Jordan: yes — can you upload the sample?
[05:56] Priya: i'll upload today. also want results for both rerank-only and full hosted retrieval+rerank.
[06:03] Maya: we'll run both. i'll include p50/p95, token counts, and cost per 1k with candidate sizes 20/100/200.
[06:15] [10m of demo interaction - clipped in transcript]
[16:20] Alex: some of the transcription here is odd, sorry, but question — do you support streaming rerank responses or is it all-or-nothing?
[16:29] Maya: rerank typically returns a ranked list, you can stream token-level generative responses in other endpoints, but for reranking it's a sync call.
[16:38] Priya: any hooks for passing embeddings metadata (e.g., doc timestamps, quality scores) into rerank?
[16:44] Maya: yes, metadata can be passed as payload and used in rerank prompts. we also support passing structured tool calls if you want side-channel signals.
[16:55] Carlos: what about model drift — do you offer monitors?
[17:00] Maya: Optimize has quality monitors, regression alerts tied to your eval sets and prompt sets. you can trigger rollover or automatic rollback policies.
[17:10] Jordan: quick note on integration patterns: minimal integration is calling embeddings + storing vectors, then you call search + rerank for top-K. alternative is delegate retrieval to your vector DB and use our rerank API. both are supported.
[17:25] Alex: any reference for sample code? we use python and node.
[17:29] Jordan: yes, we'll send quickstart repo links for python/node, and a snippet showing top-k call plus rerank.
[17:37] Priya: latency parity question again — if we keep vector store in our cluster in the same VPC as our app and call Redwood rerank over the internet, will that be a major variable?
[17:46] Maya: depends on hop. 20–60ms is typical cross-region. if you need sub-100ms total, consider colocating or Private deployment.
[17:58] Alex: what about throttling? if we hit rate limits during pilot can we request raises?
[18:03] Jordan: yes, for pilots we can temporarily increase quotas; production should have committed tiers.
[18:10] [brief pause while screenshare switches]
[18:22] Maya: showing Optimize's candidate size sweep — here's a plot of MRR vs candidate_size and cost. you can choose operating point.
[18:35] Alex: that's exactly the type of insight we need. are there built-in connectors to s3 or airflow for batch embedding updates?
[18:43] Maya: we provide ingestion connectors for S3 and GCS, and APIs that work smoothly with airflow tasks. for incremental updates you can call batch embeddings endpoint.
[18:55] Priya: how long does a 5GB batch take on hosted?
[19:00] Maya: depends on concurrency, but ballpark hours; we recommend a dedicated batch window or use our Dedicated cluster for faster throughput. we'll include guidance for your sample size.
[19:12] Carlos: on the security docs, can you share SOC2 and network diagrams asap?
[19:16] Jordan: yes will attach SOC2 report and the network architecture for hosted and private.
[19:21] Alex: ok logistics — we want to see the bench by monday and decide on pilot next tuesday.
[19:27] Jordan: sounds good. Maya, anything else on the tech side?
[19:30] Maya: nothing major, just one note — when you share sample data, include a small labeled set for eval so we can produce apples-to-apples metrics.
[19:38] Priya: will do. also cc'ing Eng manager so they can follow the pilot.
[19:42] Jordan: cool. to wrap up i'll summarize next steps in an email: pricing sheet, SOC2 & security docs, quickstart links, and we'll run the benchmark.
[19:52] Alex: thanks everyone. good session.
[19:55] Carlos: thanks.
[20:00] Jordan: thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
